edges.description: Without DHRS3 returning retinaldehyde to retinol, more retinaldehyde is irreversibly oxidised to all-trans retinoic acid.
Less retinaldehyde is reduced back to retinol, lowering retinol and retinyl ester levels.
Excess RA activates RAR/RXR heterodimers and alters transcription of RA target genes in the embryo.
Excess RA signalling at the coronal suture promotes premature osteogenic differentiation of suture mesenchyme.
Excess RA during heart development disrupts atrial and ventricular septation and outflow tract formation.
Excess RA signalling disturbs vertebral development.
Excess osteogenesis at the coronal suture closes it prematurely.
Proposed by analogy with the mouse vertebral phenotype; spinal imaging of patients has not been reported.
Embryonic RA is raised to a degree comparable with the plasma RA rise in patients.

edges.limitations: The mouse is a complete null, while patients carry hypomorphic alleles; the mouse defects (VSD, absent atrial septation, double-outlet right ventricle) are more severe than the mainly atrial septal defects in patients.
Null embryos die before birth, so only coronal suture narrowing and, in one of six embryos, bone growth across the suture can be observed; established craniosynostosis cannot be assessed.

nodes.description: Atrial septal defect in both index-family siblings and one p.(Val171Met) homozygote.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, both affected siblings in family 1 share a similar presentation of congenital anomalies, including coronal craniosynostosis, septal heart defects, and scoliosis

nodes.description: Abnormal vertebral development. Dhrs3-null mouse embryos show fusion of the first two cervical vertebrae, a classic sign of RA excess. Whether the scoliosis seen in every patient arises from comparable vertebral malformation has not been reported; the edge to scoliosis is inferred from the parallel the authors draw between the human and mouse phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: Unilateral or bilateral fusion of the first 2 cervical vertebrae, which was observed in every Dhrs3−/− embryo examined (n = 6), is a classic feature of excessive RA signaling.

nodes.description: Defective septation of the developing heart. Dhrs3-null mouse embryos have membranous ventricular septal defects, absent atrial septation and double-outlet right ventricle; patients mainly have atrial septal defects.

evidence.reference_title: The retinaldehyde reductase DHRS3 is essential for preventing the formation of excess retinoic acid during embryonic development.
evidence.snippet: Consequently, Dhrs3 ablation results in heart septation defects, both VSD and ASD, and defects in the outflow tract formation, DORV, and are nonviable.

nodes.description: Structural heart defects in four of five individuals: atrial septal defects in three, and aortic pseudo-coarctation with aortic root dilatation and absent pericardium in one.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: manifested a congruent phenotype, including coronal craniosynostosis, dysmorphic facial features, congenital heart disease (4/5 individuals)

nodes.description: Premature osteogenic differentiation and bone formation at the coronal suture. In RA-exposed suture mesenchyme this runs through BMP-SMAD1/5/9 activation, which Noggin can block. Dhrs3-null mouse embryos die before birth, but at E17.5 they already show coronal suture narrowing and, in one of six embryos, bone growth across the suture.

evidence.reference_title: PLGA-based control release of Noggin blocks the premature fusion of cranial sutures caused by retinoic acid.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, BMP signal pathway was found to be activated by atRA, as seen from increased expression of BMPR-2 and pSMAD1/5/9.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: We observed frequent unilateral (left sided) narrowing of the coronal suture (asterisk) in E17.5 Dhrs3−/− embryos compared with Dhrs3+/+ (Figures 7G-J) and in 1 case, considerable bone growth across the coronal suture (arrow) (n = 1/6).

nodes.description: Unilateral or bilateral coronal craniosynostosis, present in all five individuals carrying the pathogenic alleles; one also had unilateral lambdoid involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: The 3 individuals in families 3 and 4 homozygous for p.(Val171Met) have strikingly similar features to the siblings in family 1, including unilateral or bilateral coronal craniosynostosis (3 of 3 individuals)

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: we provide evidence that homozygosity for the 5‘UTR (family 1) and p.(Val171Met) (families 3 and 4) variants in DHRS3 together define a novel RA embryopathy of humans

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic DHRS3 variants reduce the NADPH-dependent reduction of all-trans retinaldehyde to retinol. The index-family deletion removes the promoter and part of the 5'-UTR and leaves 2-10% residual transcript; the p.(Val171Met) substitution destabilises the Rossmann fold and reduces catalytic activity. Complete loss is not seen in patients, and complete loss in mice is lethal before birth.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: Transcription of DHRS3 in whole blood cells from 2 homozygotes for the promoter/5'-untranslated region deletion was 90% to 98% reduced.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
evidence.snippet: Cells transfected with a DHRS3-Val171Met construct exhibited reduced retinaldehyde reduction capacity compared with wild-type, yielding reduced retinol and elevated RA

nodes.description: Global Dhrs3-null mice raise embryonic RA by about 40% and die in late gestation with septal and outflow tract heart defects, cleft palate, cervical vertebral fusion, porous parietal bones and coronal suture narrowing. Restricting maternal dietary vitamin A over successive generations rescues the cardiac defects and allows survival to adulthood.

Elevated all-trans retinoic acid (RA) formation. Patients homozygous for the pathogenic alleles have plasma RA 72-151% above unaffected relatives, above the family-specific upper limit, and Dhrs3-null mouse embryos carry about 40% more RA than wild-type littermates. The magnitude depends on dietary vitamin A, which supplies the retinol precursor.

evidence.reference_title: The retinaldehyde reductase DHRS3 is essential for preventing the formation of excess retinoic acid during embryonic development.
evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate that the reduction of retinaldehyde by DHRS3 is critical for preventing formation of excess ATRA during embryonic development.

nodes.description: Elevated RAR/RXR-dependent transcription in embryonic tissues, the common effector of retinoic acid embryopathy. Dhrs3 is expressed predominantly in the dura mater and one osteogenic cluster of the developing coronal suture, and RA signalling in the calvaria concentrates either side of the coronal sutures.

evidence.reference_title: The retinaldehyde reductase DHRS3 is essential for preventing the formation of excess retinoic acid during embryonic development.
evidence.snippet: In summary, Dhrs3-deficient mice have disrupted retinoid homeostasis, resulting in alterations in RAR/RXR-based signaling.

evidence.snippet: Xgal (blue) staining of a representative E18.5 RARE-lacZ mouse skull provides direct visualization of RA signaling in the calvaria, concentrated in the medial and ventral regions of the frontal and parietal bones on either side of the coronal sutures

evidence.snippet: Hence, this represents a clear example of a severely hypomorphic (partial loss-of-function) variant.

nodes.description: Missense substitution of a buried Rossmann-fold valine, found homozygous in a Spanish and a Mexican family; reduces DHRS3 activity in vitro and raises patient plasma RA.
